reason: The cited evidence (E1-E4) from a single study on CoCrFeNi nanopillars supports the mechanism linking atomic-level heterogeneities to enhanced tensile ductility via twinning-dislocation synergy. However, the hypothesis applies this mechanism to a different alloy (HfZrTiTa0.53) in bulk form, with no cited evidence that such heterogeneities exist or produce the same effect in that system, nor that the predicted quantitative outcomes (yield strength >1.5 GPa, uniform elongation >20%) are supported.
premises: Chemical compositional heterogeneities at the atomic level can promote spatial and synergistic coordination of deformation twinning and dislocation slip.
This coordination leads to ultrahigh uniform tensile ductility in multi-principal element alloys.
The mechanism is effective at room temperature under tensile loading.
The mechanism can be transferred from CoCrFeNi nanopillars to bulk HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy.
